summary: FLARE is an interactive research and analysis platform designed to make spacecraft fire-safety investigations easier to explore, compare, and understand. Using NASA-related microgravity fire investigation records, FLARE organizes research data into a centralized database and provides interactive visualizations, experimental comparisons, investigation rankings, and a citation-based question-answering system. The platform helps researchers explore existing fire-safety knowledge, identify research gaps, and support future human space exploration missions to the Moon and Mars.
details:
What FLARE does:
FLARE (Fire Lab & Research Intelligence Engine) is a dynamic research intelligence dashboard that simplifies the exploration, comparison and comprehension of microgravity combustion research.
It solves the problem of extracting useful information from decades of space-based combustion investigations by assembling the available research metadata and experimental data into a structured and searchable system.

How It Works:
FLARE has four major capabilities:
1. Explore: browse combustion investigations, inspect experiment profiles, filter records, and examine research coverage.
2. Compare: Compare the investigations and available runs from their documented conditions and parameters.
3. Ask: Post research questions and get the right evidence, with source citations. The system can indicate lack of evidence, rather than inventing conclusions.
4. Data Quality: Check source verification status, missing information, validation flags and data provenance.
The system works on an evidence-first basis. It separates documented experimental conditions from genuine experimental outcomes and pinpoints research gaps.

Foundation for Data & Research:
FLARE utilises NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigation resources, including research on BASS, BASS-II, SAFFIRE, SAME, FLEX, and other combustion investigations.
The current prototype has 20 investigation records and 10 rows of BASS-II experimental test data. Not all records are independently validated. Complete experimental outcome tables and curated research findings are still to be loaded.
The present data set is related to microgravity investigations. This makes the lack of loaded lunar and Martian gravity investigation records a research gap, rather than assuming that there is evidence to the contrary.

Technology Stack:

  • Programming language: Python
  • Interface: Streamlit
  • Data processing: Pandas
  • Visualizations: Plotly
  • Database: SQLite with full-text search
  • Configuration: YAML
  • Document processing: PyPDF
  • Optional services: FastAPI and LLM integration

Innovation and Creativity:
FLARE is more than just a repository of raw research records. It combines investigation metadata, experimental conditions, source references, comparison tools and evidence retrieval in a single interface.
The key design principle behind it is transparency: users can see what evidence is available, what is missing and what cannot be verified. This system is not designed to make unsupported scientific claims or to predict fire risk.

Intended Impact:

FLARE aims to make space-based combustion research more accessible to researchers and future mission planners. By helping users understand existing research and identify knowledge gaps, it could support future investigations into spacecraft fire safety and contribute to research for safer lunar habitats and Mars missions

Explore the Live Flare Application:

https://flare-fire.streamlit.app/
